summary: The study investigates the growth kinetics of Hf silicate-like films using Hf(N(CH3)2C2H5)4 and SiH(N(CH3)2)3 precursors with H2O as an oxidant. The growth behavior is influenced by the ratio of HfO2 and SiO2 deposition cycles, and the presence of SiO2 suppresses HfO2 nucleation due to remnant Si-H bonds. The films are grown at 280°C using an ALD system with a vertical warm-wall reactor.
evidence: The growth kinetics of Hf silicate-like films, prepared using Hf /H20851N/H20849CH3/H20850/H20849C2H5/H20850/H208524 and SiH/H20851N/H20849CH3/H208502/H208523 precursors via an H2O oxidant were investigated as a function of alternating deposition of HfO2 and SiO2. The nucleation of HfO2 showed a strong dependence on the preceding growth cycles of SiO2, as evidenced by in situ medium energy ion scattering analysis. Hf coverage was reduced with an increasing ratio of SiO2 deposition cycles. The suppression of the nucleation of HfO2 is related to remnant Si-H bonds induced by the SiH /H20851N/H20849CH3/H208502/H208523 precursor after the atomic layer deposited growth of SiO2.
